static_proof.guard_intent: Mechanically enforces: reporting_reader is NOLOGIN with every role-administration attribute explicitly denied; every GRANT/ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement targets only schema reporting with only SELECT/USAGE/CONNECT, never INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/CREATE/ALL, and never schema public or any public.* relation; the migration fails closed if schema reporting is missing; the migration verifies its own grant set in-transaction before committing; the rollback drops the role and revokes every grant without touching schema reporting itself; the migration creates no schema object of any kind other than the role.

reversibility.rollback_restores_prior_behaviour_exactl: DROP OWNED BY reporting_reader + explicit REVOKEs remove every privilege this migration granted; DROP ROLE IF EXISTS removes the role itself. Schema reporting and its views (owned by UTV2-1399) are never touched -- the rollback asserts this in-transaction.
reversibility.round_trip_drill_note: No Docker or psql available locally. migration-reversibility-gate.yml replays the full migration ledger (including UTV2-1399's, which precedes this one by timestamp) on scratch postgres:16, so schema reporting exists in that drill regardless of production's current state. That drill's schema-hash comparison uses --schema=public --no-acl, which captures neither roles/grants nor schema reporting, so this migration is expected to be schema-hash-neutral there.
